name: V2.2.7
body:
# V2.2.7

**Slash commands right away, and the last native dropdowns.** The `/` menu now works the moment a saved session opens, and the remaining plain system dropdowns follow the skins. Everything from [2.2.6](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.2.6) is included.

## `/` works before the first message

A saved session opens without starting Pi until you send something, and until then the `/` menu stayed empty. Now `/login`, `/logout`, `/compact` and `/goalmax` are always listed, and skills, prompt templates and extension commands come from any running session of the same project, or from the last list seen for it. Right after Fate UI starts, before any session in the project has run, only the built-in commands are listed.

## Every dropdown follows the skin

These used the operating system's plain dropdown and now use the skinned one in Default, Angelcore and M3 Expressive:

- **Session**, **Model** and **Thinking** in the web workspace header.
- **Device preset** in the browser's device toolbar. The browser page steps aside while its list is open, so the list is never hidden behind the page.
- **Requested permission** in the web control panel.
- **Status** of a GoalMax task.

name: V2.2.6
body:
# V2.2.6

**Compact on demand, and every window in every skin.** A new `/compact` command compacts the conversation from the composer, Windows recovers a stale lock after a crash even when the process ID was reused, and Memory Learning and the other windows that ignored the skins now look like the rest of the app in Default, Angelcore and M3 Expressive. Two new color themes are included. Everything from [2.2.5](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.2.5) is included.

## `/compact` in the composer

- Type `/compact` to compact the current conversation, or `/compact <instructions>` to tell the summary what to keep. It is listed in the slash menu.
- Progress and the result show in the timeline the same way as **Compact session context** in a session's ⋯ menu, including a failed compaction such as a conversation that is too short.
- `/compact` is sent on its own: with an image, a browser annotation, a session reference or a pinned lesson attached it asks you to remove them first. It is refused while a reply is streaming; send it once the reply finishes.
- From a browser or remote client, `/compact` with attached text files is refused and the files are kept, so attached text can never become the compaction instructions.

## Windows lock recovery after a crash

When Fate UI was killed and Windows later gave a new process the same process ID, the old lock looked as if its owner was still running, and every start failed until the lock was removed by hand. Fate UI now compares the process start time with the lock's start time, so a stale lock is recovered while a lock held by a running Fate UI is never taken. The check runs Windows PowerShell with its own module path, the same way the private-folder checks do, so a PowerShell 7 install cannot break it.

## Windows that follow the skins

- **Memory Learning** is rebuilt from the same parts as Settings: a header with close, grouped rows, a real select for the selection mode, Profile and Project as a scope switch, and Lessons, Drafts and Recent use as view chips. The three paragraphs of explanation are now a short status card, and "Learning is off" comes with an **Open Settings** button. Deleting a lesson now asks for confirmation.
- **Profile** and **Project** replace GLOBAL and PROJECT in Memory Learning, in **Settings → Memory Learning** and in the composer's Memory Learning button.
- **Agent workspace** uses the skin's select for the integration method and bracketed actions in Angelcore. It still says plainly that a worktree is a separate checkout, not a security sandbox.
- **Connect a provider** and the provider models list use the skin's buttons for retry, cancel and enable or disable all, with bracketed labels in Angelcore.
- **Edit goal** and **Clear this goal?** show their description as small muted text instead of heading-sized text, use bracketed actions in Angelcore, and **Cancel & clear** is readable in M3 Expressive.
- Angelcore: the image viewer is a transparent canvas over the dark backdrop again instead of a filled card.

## New themes

**Dark Standard** and **Light Standard** are neutral warm-gray palettes with a white or near-black accent. Pick them in **Settings → Skins → Palette**.

name: V2.2.5
body:
# V2.2.5

**Agents that really turn off, and a polish pass.** Turning an Agent off now stops its session instead of hiding the chat, Agent chats hand work off and answer right away, and music pauses while you dictate. A full review of the app also fixed bugs in Agent runs, focus and scrolling, removed work done on every streamed update, and cleaned up all three bundled skins. Everything from [2.2.4](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.2.4) is included.

## Turning an Agent off stops it

- **Turn off** on an Agent's row aborts a reply in progress, cancels the Agent's runs and ends its session. The composer is disabled and nothing can be sent into the chat until you turn the Agent back on. The saved conversation stays readable.
- Deleting an Agent stops its session the same way.
- A run that was still starting when you turned its Agent off kept going with its 30-minute limit. It now stops as soon as it has started. If a run fails right after its session starts, that session is stopped too instead of running on with nothing tracking it.
- Ctrl+N, the **New session** button in the collapsed sidebar and the command palette could replace an Agent's chat with a separate session. All three are now unavailable while an Agent chat is open, as the button in the expanded sidebar already was.

## Agent chats delegate and answer right away

An Agent's chat now works as an orchestrator. It sends project work to a run with `run_in_project` and anything else to a child agent with `spawn_agent`. The child uses the Agent's own model and effort unless you ask for different ones. The Agent replies at once with a short line and reports results in the chat when they arrive.

## Music pauses while you dictate

Chromium's echo cancellation treated the music dock's audio as echo and suppressed your voice along with it, so transcription failed while music played. The dock now pauses while the microphone records and resumes afterwards if it was playing.

## Less work while a reply streams

- The main process built the full session state twice for every event batch, which arrives up to every 32 ms during a reply. The crash-recovery snapshot now reads the state only when it writes, at most every 750 ms, and the other lookups read the session and project directly.
- Terminal keystrokes and resizes no longer build the full session state to check which project the terminal belongs to.
- The composer, the Changes panel, the agent tree in **Run → Agents** and the conversation timeline no longer re-render for updates they do not show. The closed music dock no longer re-renders four times a second while music plays.
- Collapsed tool cards render a short preview of their input instead of the whole input, which can be tens of kilobytes for a file write.
- The sidebar and **Run → Monitor** stop refreshing every 15 seconds while the window is hidden or minimized, and the sidebar refreshes once when the window comes back.

## Fixes

- Page Up and the arrow keys in the conversation no longer snap back to the bottom while a reply streams.
- A remote image you allowed with **Load remote image** no longer disappears again on the next streamed update.
- Closing the command palette, the goal editor or the provider dialog returns focus to where it was, and **Focus composer** in the palette now focuses the composer.
- Rejecting a hunk that can no longer be reverted shows an error instead of failing silently.
- **Settings → System** no longer stays on its loading placeholder when you switch sections before diagnostics finish loading.
- Relative times in the Agents tab and the Inbox update every minute instead of freezing.
- A project's session count in the sidebar no longer drops to 0 while its sessions are still listed.
- Dragging a pane divider no longer restarts the layout transition on every mouse move, so panes follow the pointer.
- The cancel button of a voice model download no longer flickers when you hover it.
- Copying the same message or code block twice keeps the checkmark for the full time.

## Skins

- Long notifications, such as git push output, stop at the window edge and scroll instead of running off screen.
- Settings selects keep their width next to long descriptions. Before, the background **Effect** select could shrink and cut off its value. The background **Effect** and **Image strength** selects now match the others in Compact mode, and the background section lines up with the rows above it.
- Long branch names in the branch menu, and long details in Activity and the Inbox, end with "…" instead of being cut off mid-letter.
- Angelcore: branch menu rows use the skin's row height and text size again. The copy action confirms with `[done]` instead of `[copied]`, so the actions next to it do not move.
- M3 Expressive: the Memory Learning button in the composer is round like the buttons next to it.
- Web workspace: the connection panel's buttons and fields use the panel color instead of black, which made them unreadable on light palettes.

## Wording

- Sign-in errors point to `/login` and **Settings → Agent → Add provider** instead of a **Connect your AI** button that is hidden once a project is open. An empty session list without a provider says to type `/login`.
- The Agent, routine and watch editors say what is wrong, such as "Add a name." or "Use 1 to 10080 minutes.", instead of generic validation text.
- The `/goalmax` entry in the command menu shows `/goalmax <objective>`, and its errors say "session" instead of "thread".
- Messages about activity that is no longer kept use plain words instead of internal terms.
- Labels: **Check for updates**, **Use skin defaults**, **Create team**, and `Ctrl/⌘ Enter to send` to match Settings.

name: V2.2.4
body:
# V2.2.4

**Agent Teams fixes and fewer limits.** Subagent results now always reach the parent, agent limits are lifted, and a model asking for a thinking level it cannot use no longer loses the whole batch. Context also shows tokens per second, and multi-question prompts can go back. Everything from [2.2.3](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.2.3) is included.

## Subagent results always arrive

- A settled agent's final answer stays readable after it is released. `inspect_agent` returns it for any owned descendant, and `wait_agent` returns the latest answer of every child that changed, up to 16,000 characters each. Before, `inspect_agent` on a released child only said it was released and `wait_agent` listed paths.
- In `agent_workflow`, the graph-level `notifyParent` now carries the result text of every node that has no `notifyParent` of its own, up to 6,000 characters per node and 24,000 in total. Before, it only said the graph had settled, so a workflow set to `immediate` with default nodes silently dropped all eight answers. A node with its own `notifyParent` still delivers separately, so nothing arrives twice.
- The `notifyParent`, `wait_agent` and `inspect_agent` descriptions and the agent catalog now say where results come from.

## Thinking levels no longer abort a batch

A `thinkingLevel` the selected model does not support is clamped to the nearest level it does support, and a non-reasoning model uses `off`. Before, admission rejected the launch with zero work done, even when the catalog listed the level. A level inherited from the caller is clamped the same way.

## Fewer agent limits

- Agents nest up to depth 16 instead of 2.
- `agent_workflow` runs every ready node in parallel by default. `maxConcurrency` defaults to 256 instead of 4 and still works as an upper bound.
- Teams saved with the old limits (16 nodes, 3 active turns, depth 2) pick up the new ones on restore.
- The agent catalog no longer tells models about a 3-turn or 16-node ceiling that was already gone. That stale text made models plan around limits that did not exist.

Still in place: one writer at a time per shared checkout (agents in separate worktrees write in parallel), 32 KiB per team message, 256 nodes per workflow graph and 5 minutes per `wait_agent` call.

## Context shows tokens per second

**System → Context** has a fourth field next to Session tokens, Cache coverage and Session cost: **Latest t/s**, the output tokens per second of the latest response. The time runs from the start of the response to when it was saved, so it includes time to first token and reads a little lower than pure decode speed. It shows "—" until a response completes or when no usable timing exists.

## Questions can go back

In a multi-question prompt, **Previous** and **Next** buttons let you return to an earlier question and change your answer. The earlier answer is shown selected, and a typed answer is kept in the field.

name: V2.2.3
body:
# V2.2.3

**Hotfix for 2.2.2 "SpaceTime".** It fixes the computer use overlay that appeared at startup and could not be brought back, the lock-out where every message failed with `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, and GoalMax gates that were written as rules but never enforced. It also moves to Pi 1.4.0. Everything from [2.2.2](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.2.2) is included.

> [!WARNING]
> GoalMax in 2.2.2 is broken. A long goal fills the lifecycle index, after which Fate UI refuses every prompt, queue, stop and new session with `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE: Lifecycle checkpoint could not be saved`, and the agent ignores the plan, sync and delegation contract because nothing enforced it. Both are fixed here; install this build before starting another goal.

## Computer use overlay

- The frame and the **Computer use** pill no longer appear when Fate UI starts. They appear when the agent performs its first `computer` action and disappear when the turn ends or after 15 seconds without an action.
- **Stop** on the pill, and **Alt+Shift+Esc** (**⌥⇧Esc** on macOS), now stop the running session exactly like the Stop button in the composer. Computer use itself stays on, so the agent can use the `computer` tool again in the next turn. In 2.2.2 the Stop button turned computer use off while the switch still showed it as on, and the agent reported "Computer use is off" until a restart.
- The computer use switch in the permission menu and in **Settings → Workspace** reads the real state of the service, and it is locked while a session is running. Turn it off between turns.
- The **Stop** label is centred in its button.

## Lock-out after `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`

The lifecycle index `~/.pi/fateGUI/lifecycle/v1/status-v1.jsonl` was capped at 512 records and 2 MB, and every ordinary run added two. Once full, each write failed, the recovery coordinator marked storage unhealthy, and all new work was refused until the file was edited by hand.

- When the index reaches its limit, Fate UI compacts it: one record per execution identity is kept, and the oldest plain run records are dropped until the index is at half its limit. Team, task, goal, worktree and command records are never dropped. The file is rewritten atomically; prior records are retained if the rewrite fails.
- A copy that is already locked recovers by itself: restart Fate UI, and the first new run compacts the full index. No file needs to be edited.

## GoalMax gates are enforced

The gateway contract is checked when a tool is called, not after the turn:

- **Plan gate.** `write`, `edit`, `pdf_fill`, `pdf_create`, `computer`, `bash` (other than read-only inspection) and delegation tools are rejected until the task plan is captured with `goalmax_report`.
- **Sync gate.** The first workspace change or delegation of a turn is rejected until the turn has called `goalmax_status` or `goalmax_report`.
- **Delegation gate.** With the default agent strategy, the root agent plans, delegates, verifies and reports; its own `write` and `edit` calls are rejected. Set the goal's agent strategy to off for root-only work.

A rejected call returns the gate and the exact next step to the model. The post-turn check that blocks a goal on a slipped violation is unchanged.

## Pi 1.4.0

Pi SDK and Pi Durable move from 1.3.0 to [1.4.0](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v1.4.0). Fixes that reach Fate UI:

- Compaction and branch summaries use the model's output limit, so they no longer fail with "generation hit the token cap" when reasoning uses most of the old fixed limit.
- A session no longer breaks after recovering from a response cut off at the output limit. Previously every later request was rejected by the provider.
- Automatic retry now covers more gateway upstream failures, `stream disconnected before completion` from Codex CLI proxies, and transient Google Vertex sign-in refresh errors. Digits inside request ids are no longer mistaken for HTTP status codes.
- Whitespace-only tool output, such as a bare line break from `bash`, no longer makes OpenAI and Google requests fail with a 400.
- GitHub Copilot requests that are too large, for example with many images, are treated as context overflow and compacted instead of failing with HTTP 413.
- The `grep` tool ignores `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, so a user ripgrep config can no longer turn regex searches into literal ones.
- New models: `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, and the `xhigh` thinking level for Grok 4.3 and 4.5 on xAI.

> [!NOTE]
> With native Durable storage on, the first start of this version migrates the storage database to a new schema. Earlier Fate UI versions cannot open it afterwards, so a native-Durable profile cannot go back to 2.2.2 or older. Profiles with the default storage are not affected.

## Known limits

- **The Node companion is not among these release files.** Its builder supports Linux x64 only. Build it from this tag with the [package guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.3/build/server-package/README.md). It needs Node 22.19 or later.
- No automated check drives a real mouse, a global hotkey or an elevated relaunch, so computer use is not covered by the test matrix on any platform.
- Computer use on Linux needs X11 or XWayland.

## Installation

| Platform | Architecture | Formats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | x64 | EXE |
| macOS | Apple Silicon and Intel | DMG, PKG |
| Linux | x64 | AppImage, DEB |

Installers remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized. Verify your download with `SHA256SUMS`; a checksum does not replace code signing.

[Setup guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.3/docs/v2/quickstart.md) · [Security and limits](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.3/docs/v2/security-and-limits.md) · [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.3/docs/v2/troubleshooting.md) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/issues)

name: V2.2.2 - SpaceTime
body:
# V2.2.2 - SpaceTime

**The first stable release since 1.1.1, and the one where the agent gets hands.** SpaceTime lets the agent see your screen and use your mouse and keyboard. It also brings everything from the 2.0 and 2.2 betas to the stable channel, plus branch worktrees and long chats that open fast.

Agents become assistants you talk to. Fate can run on another machine and be used from a browser. Pi moves from 0.85 to 1.3. The agent can now see your screen and use your mouse and keyboard when you allow it.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Back up `~/.pi` before you install this over 1.1.x. Check for Updates offers this build to stable copies. Saved Agents become global, and the Agents library from 1.1 is replaced by one chat per Agent (see [Upgrading](#upgrading-from-11x)).

**Size of this release:** more than 100 commits and about 835 changed files since 1.1.1. The 2.0.0-beta, 2.0.1-beta and 2.2.0-beta changes are all included; their pages stay up for the details.

## Computer use: the agent can use your computer

![Fate UI while computer use is running: a purple frame around the screen, the Computer use pill with its Stop button at the top, and the agent's cursor labelled Click](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/ad3dec02c14605adc38b31a99d5dce1f9c3cac52/screenshots/computer-use-overlay.png)

*While the agent is acting, a frame lights up around every screen, a pill shows Computer use with its stop shortcut and a Stop button, and the agent's cursor is labelled with what it is doing. The frame, pill and cursor are the real overlay markup from the app, drawn over a Fate UI window.*

The agent can take screenshots and drive the mouse and keyboard through a new `computer` tool: click, double and triple click, drag, scroll, type, key chords, hold a key, zoom into a region, and pick a display.

- **Off until you turn it on.** Use the switch in the permission menu of the composer or **Settings → Workspace → Computer use**. It only works in a **Full access** session; turning it on from the composer moves the session to Full access.
- **Always stoppable.** An overlay shows when the agent is acting, with a Stop button, and **Alt+Shift+Esc** (**⌥⇧Esc** on macOS) turns it off from anywhere. It also turns off when the last window closes.
- **Fate UI relaunches elevated** (a UAC prompt on Windows, an administrator prompt on macOS, `pkexec` on Linux) so the agent can reach every window. The whole app, its shell tool and its child processes then run with administrator rights, and the choice is remembered for the next start. On Windows the UAC prompt on the secure desktop is also switched off while computer use is on, so the agent can see it, and it is put back when you turn computer use off. Only turn it on if you accept that.
- **macOS** asks for Accessibility and Screen Recording permission first. **Linux** needs an X11 or XWayland display; pure Wayland is not supported yet.
- Agent runs started from an Agent chat do not get the tool.

![The permission menu of the composer with the Computer use switch below Read only, Edit files and Full access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/ad3dec02c14605adc38b31a99d5dce1f9c3cac52/screenshots/computer-use-switch.png)

*The switch sits in the permission menu of the composer, under the three levels. It is off by default.*

## Also new since 2.2.0-beta

### Branches in their own worktree

- Picking a branch while you have uncommitted changes now opens it in a managed worktree and leaves your changes on the current branch, instead of failing.
- A branch that already has a worktree is listed with a **worktree** tag and opens that worktree.
- Each local branch has a delete button with a confirmation. Deleting a branch also removes its worktree. It refuses when a running session uses that worktree, or when the branch is checked out in the primary worktree.
- The picker no longer hides branches that are checked out in another worktree.

### Long chats open fast

- A long session opens on its latest window of history. Scroll up and earlier messages load in pages, instead of being cut off for good.
- Images outside the recent budget stay as placeholders and load when you open them.
- Images you attach or receive are grouped into two-per-row tiles that open the full-size viewer. Tool-result images stay hidden while the tool card is collapsed.

### Sessions and sidebar

- Delete a saved session of any project straight from the sidebar, not only of the open one. A project in the background keeps running.
- A background project whose selected session you delete closes cleanly first.

### Fixed in this stretch

- Agent journal writes that Windows reported as busy are retried.
- The Agents tests and the Settings saved-toast checks no longer fail on slow runners.
- CI takes the pnpm version from `package.json`.
- A duplicate `deleteSession` branch in the runtime router is gone; the one that ran before and the one meant to run now agree.

## Agents, rebuilt

An Agent is a saved persona with exactly one conversation of its own, like a personal assistant chat. Agents are global and no longer saved per project.

- **One chat per Agent.** Select **Agents** in the sidebar and **+** to create one.
- **Work in your projects.** Ask for work in a trusted project. The Agent starts a background **run** with `run_in_project`, answers right away, and continues when the run finishes. Up to four runs are active at once; each stops after 30 minutes. **Open run** shows it.
- **Inbox and notifications.** Finished, failed and interrupted runs and Routine messages land in a per-Agent inbox behind the bell, with **Unread** and **Read all**. Desktop notifications fire while Fate UI is not focused; **Mute notifications** turns them off per Agent.
- **Gmail and Google Calendar.** With your own Google OAuth client (**Settings → Agent → Google**), an Agent can search and read mail and read your primary calendar. Sending mail and changing events waits for your answer in the chat. The client secret and sign-in are encrypted with the operating system's key store, and every decision is written to `google/receipts.jsonl`.
- **Watches.** Check a public page on an interval for any change, text appearing or disappearing, or a US dollar price crossing a threshold. Checks run without the model; only a hit posts into the chat.
- **Routines** post a message into the Agent's chat on an interval.
- **Memory.** The `remember` tool saves what you state as a pending Memory Learning draft. Nothing is used until you approve it.
- **Tone and avatar**, a live `fate_capabilities` list so an Agent can walk you through what is not set up, and one permission setting shared by the chat and the card.

## Web, PDFs and file search

Root sessions, Agent chats and Agent runs get these at every permission level:

- `web_search` (Parallel's free Search MCP; turn it off in **Settings → Agent → Web search**) and `web_fetch`, which refuses private, loopback and cloud metadata addresses, also after DNS and redirects.
- `pdf_read`; with Edit files or Full access also `pdf_fill` and `pdf_create`.
- `grep`, `find` and `ls` at Read only and Edit files too, confined to the project.

## Run Fate where the code lives

Fate 2 splits a *host* that runs Pi from *clients* that show it.

- **`fate-server`** is a plain Node process with no window. It owns Pi, your registered workspaces and the provider keys. A run on the host continues after you close the client. Commands: `init`, `serve`, `web`, `provider login`, `auth-code`, `access-key create`, `doctor`, `migrate`.
- **Browser workspace** with chat, context, GoalMax and tasks, Agent Teams, Monitor, files, Git, saved history, permission requests and an optional terminal. Login is a one-use code, then an HttpOnly session cookie with CSRF protection. The host listens on `127.0.0.1` only.
- **Desktop app as a remote client** over SSH, with host key pinning (**Settings → Hosts** or `fate connect PROFILE`). A failed connection never starts a local agent in its place.
- **Observers and one controller.** A client claims a bounded control lease; control never raises the permission. After a lost connection the client shows the last known state as stale and reviews the original request instead of sending it again.
- **One owner per profile**, with recovery after a crash or power loss. Optional `native-durable` SQLite storage and `fate-server migrate` with a verified backup and a rollback. Default storage is unchanged.

## One orchestration engine

GoalMax, Agent Teams, Automations and Memory Learning now share one path. **Agent Teams is the only executor** for child sessions. A busy Team saves its state once per change instead of on every event (one child with 300 tool calls went from 706 saved snapshots, 78.8 MiB, to 5). Idle stays idle: Routines sleep until their next run, and GoalMax skips child bookkeeping while no goal is open.

## Hooks, Code Intelligence, review and cost

- **Hooks** (**Settings → Hooks**) run your shell commands before a tool call, after a result, when the agent stops and at session start. Exit code 2 blocks, adds to the result, or sends the agent back to work.
- **Code Intelligence** connects language servers and gives the agent `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_definition`, `lsp_references` and `lsp_symbols`. Every `write` and `edit` result carries the file's fresh errors.
- **Checkpoints and Rewind** on every Activity ledger row; **hunk review** with Keep and Reject in the Review Runway.
- **Pull requests:** `git_push` (refuses `main` and `master`), `pr_create` and `pr_status`; a **branch chip** with `git_branch` for the agent.
- **Usage and budget** in **Settings → Usage**, a **context inspector** beside the composer, **tool search**, and optional **Codemode**.
- **Reasoning slider** in the model popover.

## Pi SDK 1.3, MCP and more

- **Pi 0.85 → 1.3.** Resumed sessions keep their tools, model switches no longer leak old thinking, OpenRouter lists only your models, Kimi Code and Azure are updated (Azure is now one provider called `azure`; sign in again if you used it), and many provider and retry fixes landed. A prompt is either admitted by Pi or refused.
- **MCP servers** (**Settings → MCP**), **Switch from Pi Terminal**, **questions from the agent**, a **Monitor** panel and standard Pi 1.0 themes.
- **Real tool times** measured by Pi, and a stopped run stays stopped.
- **Settings → System → Beta branch** lets Check for Updates also offer pre-releases.
- Sessions larger than 128 MiB open and are never shortened.

## Fixed since 1.1.1

- The app could fail to quit; push-to-talk now runs its keyboard hook in a helper process and cannot freeze the app.
- The music player reported a missing yt-dlp when the bundled one needed more than five seconds to start.
- The Git view could show a status that was read before the agent's latest edit.
- Changes panel errors during a project switch, a tooltip covering neighboring controls, ledger rows showing after trust was lost, narrow inspector tabs, panel splitters, search field focus outlines and Monaco fallback workers.
- The installers were missing 165 runtime libraries; the Windows `fate` launcher failed with several Node installations and under the default script policy.

## Upgrading from 1.1.x

- Saved Agents are available everywhere. Earlier Agent home chats stay as normal sessions in their projects, and each Agent starts a fresh conversation. Automation files are not deleted.
- Azure users sign in again.

## Known limits

- **The Node companion is not among these release files.** Its builder supports Linux x64 only. Build it from this tag with the [package guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.2/build/server-package/README.md). It needs Node 22.19 or later.
- The network client has no built-in browser, file reveal, voice, hotkeys or rich media, and it cannot commit, revert, fetch, pull or push. [Full table](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.2/docs/v2/current-status.md#capability-matrix)
- No automated check drives a real mouse, a global hotkey or an elevated relaunch, so computer use and push-to-talk are not covered by the test matrix on any platform.
- Computer use on Linux needs X11 or XWayland.

## Installation

| Platform | Architecture | Formats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | x64 | EXE |
| macOS | Apple Silicon and Intel | DMG, PKG |

name: V2.2.0-beta - Radian
body:
# V2.2.0-beta - Radian

**Agents become assistants you talk to.** Each Agent now has one ongoing chat that starts work in your projects, reads your mail and calendar, searches the web, watches pages and reports back through an inbox and notifications. Underneath, every kind of background work runs on one engine, Pi moves to 1.3, and Fate gains hooks, language servers, rewind, hunk review and usage tracking.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a **pre-release for beta testers**, like 2.0.1-beta. Back up `~/.pi` before you install it over an existing installation. Installed stable copies are not offered this build, and 2.0.x beta copies are not offered it automatically either; download it below. From this build on, **Settings → System → Beta branch** lets Check for Updates offer later pre-releases. To leave the beta, uninstall it and install the stable release again.

Everything in [2.0.1-beta](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.0.1-beta) is included. This page lists what changed after it.

## Agents, rebuilt

An Agent is now a saved persona with exactly one conversation of its own, like a personal assistant chat. Agents are global: they are no longer saved per project.

- **One chat per Agent.** Select **Agents** in the sidebar and **+** to create one. Its conversation runs in a folder Fate UI owns and is not listed under any project.
- **Work in your projects.** Ask for work in a trusted project, for example "check why the build fails in fateUI". The Agent starts a background **run** with `run_in_project` and answers right away. When the run finishes, its result comes back into the chat and the Agent continues from there. A run is a normal conversation in that project, so it can use Agent Teams, GoalMax and Memory Learning, and **Open run** shows it. Up to four runs are active at once, and each stops after 30 minutes.
- **Inbox and notifications.** Finished, failed and interrupted runs and Routine messages land in a per-Agent inbox behind the bell in the Agents toolbar, with **Unread** and **Read all**. While Fate UI is not focused, every finished or failed run raises a desktop notification. **Mute notifications** turns them off for one Agent.
- **Status under the name.** In the regular sidebar each Agent shows what it is doing: the project and request of a running job, its latest unread item, **Watch paused**, its last run, or **Ready** with its permission.
- **Gmail and Google Calendar.** With your own Google OAuth client (**Settings → Agent → Google**), an Agent with Google turned on searches and reads your mail and reads your primary calendar. Sending mail and changing events shows the exact content in the chat and waits for your answer. The client secret and sign-in are encrypted with the operating system's key store, every decision is written to `google/receipts.jsonl`, and a send Google does not confirm is reported as unknown instead of retried. Full access Agents can use Google too; mail is text from other people, so give a Google Agent the shell only if you accept that risk.
- **Watches.** **+ Watch** on an Agent's card checks a public page on an interval for any change, text appearing or disappearing, or a US dollar price crossing a threshold. Checks run without the model; only a hit posts into the chat and notifies. Failed checks back off from 2 to 16 minutes, and five failures in a row pause the watch.
- **Routines** now post a message into the Agent's chat on an interval, for example "every morning, summarize my unread mail".
- **Memory.** The `remember` tool saves something you state as a pending Memory Learning draft: preferences go to your GLOBAL profile, everything else to the Agent's own PROJECT store. Nothing is used until you approve it, and a **Memory drafts** rail above the composer opens Learning. Normal chats get `remember` too.
- **Tone and avatar.** A tone of up to 500 characters is added to the Agent's system prompt, and an emoji avatar is shown in the sidebar, the chat header and on its replies.
- **Knows what it can do.** Ask an Agent what it can do, or for something it lacks. It calls `fate_capabilities`, which lists what is on right now (projects, files, shell, web, browser, Gmail and Calendar, memory, MCP servers, PDFs, images, schedules) with the exact setup steps for the rest, and walks you through them instead of saying it cannot.
- **One permission setting.** The permission menu in an Agent's chat and the one on its card are the same setting. Picking a level in the chat saves it to the Agent and restarts the idle chat at that level.

## Web, PDFs and file search for every session

Root sessions, Agent chats and Agent runs get these tools at every permission level:

- `web_search` asks Parallel's free Search MCP and returns up to 10 results with title, address and excerpt. **Settings → Agent → Web search** turns it off.
- `web_fetch` reads one public page. It refuses private, loopback and cloud metadata addresses, also after DNS resolution and redirects, and limits redirects, size and time.
- `pdf_read` returns the page count, metadata, form fields and page text. With Edit files or Full access, `pdf_fill` fills a form into a new copy and `pdf_create` renders Markdown to a PDF; each write gets a ledger row in Activity.
- `grep`, `find` and `ls` now work at Read only and Edit files too, confined to the project like `read`. An Agent run at Edit files could not list a folder before.

## One orchestration engine

GoalMax, Agent Teams, Automations and Memory Learning used to run four separate kinds of background work. They now share one path.

- **Agent Teams is the only executor** for child sessions. The old subagent engine is removed; its history still restores and renames.
- **Far less disk work.** A Team saves its state once per change instead of on every event: updates go out within 50 ms and are saved at most once a second. One busy child with 300 tool calls went from 706 saved snapshots (78.8 MiB) to 5.
- **Idle stays idle.** GoalMax skips child bookkeeping while no goal is open, Routines sleep until their next run instead of scanning the disk every 5 seconds, and Memory Learning writes nothing for turns that attach nothing.
- **Team members load hooks, Code Intelligence, usage and the context inspector**, like the root agent.

## Hooks and Code Intelligence

- **Hooks** (**Settings → Hooks**) run your own shell commands before a tool call, after a tool result, when the agent stops and when a session starts. Exit code 2 blocks the call, adds to the result, or sends the agent back to work, for example to require a passing typecheck before it stops. Hooks apply to the root agent and every Agent Team member. A hook is not a security boundary. See [Hooks](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.0-beta/docs/hooks.md).
- **Code Intelligence** (**Settings → Code Intelligence**) connects language servers and gives the agent `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_definition`, `lsp_references` and `lsp_symbols`. Every `write` and `edit` result also carries the fresh errors and warnings of that file. Defaults cover TypeScript and JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go and C/C++; Fate UI does not install the servers. See [Code Intelligence](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.0-beta/docs/code-intelligence.md).

## Review, Git and cost

- **Checkpoints and Rewind.** Every `write` and `edit` stores the file's earlier content. **Rewind** on an Activity ledger row restores every file changed from that row onward and removes files the agent created. A file changed since by a shell command, formatter or editor is skipped and named.
- **Hunk review.** In the Review Runway each hunk has **Keep** and **Reject**. Reject reverts only that hunk and drafts a feedback message with it for the agent.
- **Branches.** A branch chip in the composer switches to or creates a branch while the session is still empty. The agent uses the `git_branch` tool for the same.
- **Pull requests.** Full access sessions get `git_push` (which refuses `main` and `master`), `pr_create` and `pr_status`, which reports every check and the failed log of up to three failing runs.
- **Usage and budget.** **Settings → Usage** shows today, a 7 to 365 day window, cost per day and the top models and sessions. **Settings → Agent → Daily budget** warns after a turn once a project passes it; it is an alarm, not a hard stop.
- **Context inspector.** A `context` widget beside the composer estimates what fills the context window: system prompt, tool schemas, messages and the largest tool results.
- **Tool search** keeps rarely used tools out of the prompt until the model looks them up. **Settings → Agent → Codemode** lets the model run several tools from one script; it is off by default.
- **Reasoning slider.** The model popover shows reasoning effort as a slider; the arrow on the Reasoning row switches back to the menu.

## Pi SDK 1.3

Fate moves from Pi 1.1.0 to **Pi 1.3.0**. What that brings into Fate:

- **Resumed sessions keep their tools.** A session that loaded a tool keeps it after a restart, so Fate no longer adds every orchestration tool back by hand.
- **Clean model switches.** After you switch models, the new model no longer sees the old model's thinking as plain text in earlier replies.
- **OpenRouter** lists only the models your key may use, with that key's context size and prices.
- **Kimi Code** uses Chat Completions, and tools added during a conversation keep the prompt cache. If you override the `kimi-coding` base URL in `models.json`, it must now end in `/v1`.
- **OpenAI GPT-6** with an API key keeps the prompt cache when you change the thinking level.
- **Fewer failed turns.** "The upstream provider returned an error", "Unable to forward upstream stream" and "The service is temporarily unavailable" are retried. When Anthropic rejects the strict tool set, Pi retries once without it. Mistral streams are no longer cut off during long thinking.
- **Provider fixes:** tool calls with malformed arguments now fail and show the model what it sent, instead of running with half the fields; Claude on Anthropic and Bedrock no longer fails when an error tool result has images; Gemini 4 Argon works on Vertex; `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` uses its 500K window; Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5 accept thinking off; `auth.json` on Windows no longer fails with `EPERM` while a lock is being removed.

## Updates

- **Settings → System → Beta branch.** Off, Check for Updates offers stable releases only. On, it also offers pre-releases such as this one.
- A pre-release now says **"You are running a beta version of FateGUI."** instead of calling itself a newer or development version.

## Upgrading from 2.0.x

- Agents saved for one project are now available everywhere.
- Earlier Agent home chats stay as normal sessions in the projects where they were created. Each Agent starts a fresh conversation in its own folder.
- A Routine from an earlier version takes the prompt of its task template and starts turned off.
- Old Automations are not run. **Copy Automation** on an Agent's card turns one into a Routine that starts turned off; the original file stays unchanged.
- Agents keep their permission. Choose Full access per Agent.

## Known limits

Unchanged from [2.0.0-beta](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.0.0-beta#known-limits). In addition, Routines and Watches run only while Fate UI is open, and missed runs are skipped, not replayed. Watches read the page itself, so pages that build their text with JavaScript cannot be watched. Google shows an unverified-app warning at sign-in, because the OAuth client is your own. The Node companion is still not among the release files; build it from this tag with the [package guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.2.0-beta/build/server-package/README.md).

## Installation

| Platform | Architecture | Formats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | x64 | EXE |
| macOS | Apple Silicon and Intel | DMG, PKG |
| Linux | x64 | AppImage, DEB |

This build passed the package, install and smoke matrix on all four runners, and the exact seven-installer checksum set was verified before publishing. Installers remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized. Verify your download with `SHA256SUMS`; a checksum does not replace code signing.

# V2.0.1-beta - Radian

**A hotfix for the 2.0 beta.** Fate moves to Pi SDK 1.1, shows the real run time of each tool, and gets the fixes made since 2.0.0-beta.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a **pre-release for beta testers**, like 2.0.0-beta. Back up `~/.pi` before you install it over an existing installation. Installed stable copies are not offered this build; the stable release stays 1.1.1 until 2.0.0 is final. To leave the beta, uninstall it and install the stable release again.

Everything in [2.0.0-beta](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/releases/tag/v2.0.0-beta) is included. This page lists only what changed after it.

## Pi SDK 1.1

Fate moves from Pi 1.0.0 to **Pi 1.1.0** (Pi SDK, Pi Durable, client, protocol and server packages). What that brings into Fate:

- **Claude Haiku 5.5** is in the model list, with thinking up to `xhigh` and `max`.
- **Azure is now one provider called `azure`.** Pi renamed `azure-openai-responses`, and it now also serves Foundry Chat Completions deployments such as `azure/deepseek-v4-pro`. If you used Azure, sign in again or rename the provider key in `auth.json`, `models.json` and `settings.json`. A session that used the old name falls back to another model when you resume it.
- **Fewer failed turns.** "Selected model is at capacity", `server_busy`, Mistral `finish_reason: "error"` and stalled Bedrock HTTP/2 streams are retried instead of ending the turn. Output limits are estimated at 3.5 characters per token, so fewer requests go over the context limit.
- **Anthropic sign-in on Windows** falls back to a free local port when port 53692 is reserved, for example by Hyper-V or WSL.
- **Prompt cache:** Anthropic keeps the cache when tools change in the middle of a conversation, instead of sending the full tool list again.
- **Provider fixes:** Bedrock Claude after a changed system prompt, OpenAI models on Bedrock now follow the thinking level, Codex requests accept `headers` from `models.json`, sign-in with ChatGPT after a cancelled token refresh, and costs of long prompts on models with prompt-length pricing.
- **MCP sign-in** registers as a native client, so OpenID Connect servers no longer refuse it with `invalid_redirect_uri`.

The native durable store keeps its SQLite format. A store made by 2.0.0-beta opens unchanged, and you can go back to 2.0.0-beta with it.

## Tool times you can trust

The time on a tool card is now the time the tool really ran, measured by Pi. Before, Fate counted from when the model started its answer. On a reopened session that included the whole model response, so a one-second `read` could show half a minute. Results saved by older versions have no recorded time and keep the old estimate.

A run you stop now counts as stopped also when you stop it after its last message, for example while an extension still runs at the end of the turn. Fate takes that state from Pi instead of guessing it from the last message. A stopped project in the background is then not marked as completed, and recovery records the run as interrupted.

## Fixed since 2.0.0-beta

- **Changes panel:** opening a project could show "This project is not registered in the execution host configuration." and keep that error. A read during a project switch now waits until the switch is complete.
- **Title bar:** the execution host selector sat above the title bar and pushed the window controls to a second row. Hosts are now a Settings page (**Settings → Hosts**). The workspace header has one connection button, and only when a host is saved or connected.
- **Monitor** uses the same head, chips, rows and tags as the Activity panel, so every skin styles it. The per-source check times are in the tooltip of the footer.
- **M3 skin:** the music player is at most 360 px wide instead of the full inspector width, and its labels cannot be selected as text.
- **Compact sessions:** an empty folder shows one line instead of the large empty block.

body:
# V2.0.0-beta - Radian

**Fate UI 2.0 takes the workspace off the desktop.** Radian splits Fate into a *host* that runs Pi and *clients* that show it. The host can still be the desktop app. It can now also be a small Node process on another machine, and you work on it from the desktop app, from a browser, or through SSH.

Under that change sit a move to Pi SDK 1.0, an MCP client, questions from the agent, a Monitor dashboard, a new ownership and recovery model, and an optional SQLite storage.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a **pre-release for beta testers**. Back up `~/.pi` before you install it over an existing installation. Installed stable copies are not offered this build; the stable release stays 1.1.1 until 2.0.0 is final. To leave the beta, uninstall it and install the stable release again.

![Fate UI asking a question](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/v2.0.0-beta/screenshots/questionnaire.png)

*Actual Electron UI with a demonstration project and a test model: the agent asks, you choose.*

**Size of this release:** 38 commits, 695 changed files and about 71,700 added lines since 1.1.0, checked by more than 3,900 automated tests. The 1.1.1 hotfix for large saved sessions is included.

## Run Fate where the code lives

### The Node companion: `fate-server`

A plain Node process that owns Pi, your registered workspaces and the provider credentials. It has no window and no Electron. Closing a client does not stop it, so a run on the host continues after you close the browser or the laptop.

| Command | What it does |
| :-- | :-- |
| `fate-server init` | Creates a private profile for one trusted workspace. |
| `fate-server serve` | Runs the host without a web page. |
| `fate-server web` | Runs the host and serves the browser workspace. |
| `fate-server provider login` / `status` | Sets up the model provider on the host. Keys never pass through a browser. |
| `fate-server auth-code` | Issues a one-use login code for a browser. |
| `fate-server access-key create` | Issues a workspace-scoped credential for a desktop client. |
| `fate-server doctor` | Reports the state of a profile and changes nothing. |
| `fate-server migrate` | Moves existing state to the new storage (see below). |

A profile made this way starts with a **read-only permission maximum and the terminal off**. Both are raised only by explicit flags at `init`. The host listens on `127.0.0.1` only; there is no public mode and no mode without login. A sample systemd user unit and a [service guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.0.0-beta/docs/v2/remote-host-service.md) are included.

### The browser workspace

Open the login page, enter the one-use code, pick a registered workspace. The page is built from the same interface code as the desktop app.

- **Conversation:** chat, model and thinking level, new session, message queue, stop a run on the host, export a bounded text copy of the session.
- **Context:** attach a text file from your device, or a file of the project on the host.
- **GoalMax and tasks:** create, edit and clear a goal; create, reorder, change and clear tasks.
- **Agent Teams:** create a Team and use its lifecycle controls.
- **Monitor:** what is active and what needs attention, with a jump to the work behind a row.
- **Files:** the tree and a text preview of the registered project.
- **Git:** changed files, a diff for one file or for all, "reviewed" marks, history, and the content of one commit.
- **Saved history:** read an old conversation page by page from its start.
- **Permissions:** request a lower or a higher permission. Each change needs a one-use confirmation, and nothing above the host maximum is granted.
- **Terminal:** an optional manual shell in the browser, when the host was set up for it.

### The desktop app as a remote client

The desktop app has a new **Execution host** selector. Add an SSH host, pin its server ID, choose the private client credential, and connect — or run `fate connect PROFILE`. The app opens the tunnel through your system OpenSSH and checks the host identity, the protocol and the workspace before any work starts. An unknown or changed host key blocks the connection. A failed connection never starts a local agent in its place.

### Observers and one controller

- Every client starts as an **observer**. To change something, it claims **control**: a bounded lease that the host owns. You can renew it or release it.
- Control never raises the permission.
- When control moves to another client, requests from the earlier one are refused. A takeover is possible only when the host policy permits it.
- The selected session is shared in a workspace. When the controller selects another session, every client follows.

### After a lost connection

- What you see is the last known state, marked as possibly stale. The host can still be working.
- After a reconnect or a host restart, the client needs a fresh snapshot before it can control again. Events arrive in order behind that snapshot.
- Each change request has an ID and a recorded outcome on the host. If the answer is lost, you **review the original request**. The client does not send it again.
- Interrupted work is shown as interrupted. It is not resumed without you.

## New in the desktop app

### Pi SDK 1.0

Fate moves from Pi 0.85.1 to **Pi 1.0**. A prompt is either admitted by Pi or refused; there is no half-queued item. The standard Pi 1.0 themes and their new color format are supported.

### MCP servers

**Settings → MCP** adds a client for the Model Context Protocol, built on the official SDK. Add a local command or an HTTPS endpoint, press **Test saved server**, and turn it on. No server is on by default, and a project file cannot start one. The agent reaches MCP tools only in a Full access session. [MCP guide](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.0.0-beta/docs/mcp.md)

### Switch from Pi Terminal

**Settings → MCP → Switch from Pi Terminal** imports the provider entries and the compatible global MCP servers that Fate does not have yet. It never replaces a Fate value. A new Fate profile also starts with the model and thinking level you chose in Pi.

### Questions from the agent

Pi can stop and ask. A question card opens above the composer with two to four choices and a field for your own answer; several questions come one after the other. The agent waits for you. Skin packs can style the card.

### Monitor

One panel lists the runs, Teams, tasks and activity that are active or need attention, and opens the work behind each row. The agent can read the same dashboard with a tool. It cannot approve, stop or resume work through it.

### GoalMax and Agent Teams

- A failed verification can now be linked to a later passing run of the same check. The failure stays in the timeline as stale, with the reason.
- A sub-agent in an isolated worktree keeps its own sub-agents in that worktree, unless it asks for another workspace.
- After a restart, a saved Team is checked against its stored child sessions. Nothing is run again.

### Sessions and permissions

- Session files are read as a stream with a bounded preview. Sessions and Agent home sessions larger than 128 MiB open, and the file is never shortened.
- A saved session is tied to its real project, also when two project paths map to the same Pi folder name.
- A saved permission is restored only inside the current host limit. Unreadable or damaged permission storage blocks the agent; it never grants more access.

### Interface and launcher

- The heaviest side panels load when you first open them. If one fails to load, the other tabs stay usable.
- Push-to-talk runs its keyboard hook in a helper process. A hook that hangs cannot freeze the app; push-to-talk is then reported as unavailable.
- The `fate` launcher gains `fate connect PROFILE` and passes `init`, `serve`, `web`, `provider`, `auth-code`, `access-key` and `doctor` to an installed companion.

## Ownership, storage and recovery

### One owner for each profile

One process owns a profile and its checkouts. A second app or host on the same data is refused, so two processes cannot write the same state. After a crash, a forced quit or a power loss, the next start recovers the lock when the operating system confirms that the old process is gone. A lock is never taken because it looks old.

### Native durable storage (opt-in)

The default storage is unchanged, and existing sessions, Team history and worktrees stay as they are. A new profile can select `native-durable`: one SQLite store, through Pi's durable runtime, for the queue, the tasks and the GoalMax documents. New workflow graphs are then admitted and ordered by Pi's native tasks. A damaged or incomplete native store blocks the start; Fate never falls back to the old storage silently.

### Migration with a way back

`fate-server migrate` shows a dry run first. `prepare` writes a plan, `apply` makes a verified private backup and imports, and `rollback` returns to the original state. It does not copy provider credentials, trust or full-access grants, and it does not replay old work. [Migration procedure](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.0.0-beta/docs/v2/migration-cli.md)

### Review after an uncertain stop

If a workflow stopped in an unknown state, its history must be reviewed before new work is admitted. A storage close that could not be confirmed keeps the profile locked for an operator. An ordinary crash does not. [Workflow review](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v2.0.0-beta/docs/v2/native-workflow-review.md)

## Security defaults

- Browser login: a one-use code with a five-minute life, sent in a POST body; then an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie and a CSRF token. Requests with a wrong Host or Origin are refused.
- Profile and credential files must be private. Windows ACLs and POSIX modes are checked, and a profile that is not private is refused.
- A workspace must be registered and trusted on the host. A remote path never leaves the host, and secrets are removed from network views and host logs.
- The manual terminal is an unsandboxed shell of the host account. It needs an acknowledgement flag at `init`, current control, and a warning confirmation in the browser.
- Snapshots, lists, history pages and transport buffers have fixed limits.
- Full access stays an explicit, unsandboxed grant.

## Fixed

Defects that were in 1.1:

- The application could fail to quit: every quit started the global keyboard hook only to stop it, and that start could block for good.
- The music player reported a missing yt-dlp when the bundled one needed more than five seconds to start.
- The Git view could receive a status that was read before the agent's latest edit.
- A tooltip covered neighboring controls after a dialog returned focus to its opener.
- The Activity panel showed ledger rows for one frame after a project lost trust.
- Narrow inspector tabs, panel splitters, focus outlines on search fields, select filters after a keyboard choice, and the Monaco fallback workers.

Defects that the first V2 package runs found, fixed before this beta:

- The installers lacked 165 runtime libraries.
- The two standard Pi themes were missing on a profile without its own Pi themes.
- The browser terminal lost its connection and its control when a shell ended.
- The Windows `fate` launcher failed on a PC with several Node installations, and under the default Windows script policy.

## Beta testers: please try these

- Start again after a forced quit or a crash.
- Push-to-talk, especially on macOS and Linux. No automated check can press a global hotkey.
- Agent Teams with isolated worktrees and nested sub-agents.
- Your MCP servers, the import from Pi Terminal, and questions from the agent.

# V1.1.0 - Axiom

Fate UI 1.1 adds a local Agents library, a third built-in skin, and refinements to provider, session, and window controls.

## Agents library

Save Agent identities, reusable TaskTemplates, and interval-based Routines. Open an Agent's home conversation, start a new session, or run a TaskTemplate and review its retained history. Routines run while the app is open; missed intervals are skipped rather than replayed. Background work stays within project-trusted, read-only/edit authority. Consequential file actions require exact, single-use approval and are not silently retried after uncertain interruption.

### Upgrade from Automations

The old **Automations** tab and direct launch/edit flow are replaced by **Agents → Copy Automations**. Existing Automation files are **not deleted or rewritten**. Open and trust the original project, review each source, and copy it into a TaskTemplate. Then create or choose an Agent to run it; create a Routine only if you want a schedule. Old run counters are archived, not converted into new Run history. Copy rollback removes the copied TaskTemplate but leaves the original file intact. Back up your data before upgrading and [read the migration steps](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v1.1.0/docs/agents.md).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This changes the old Automations workflow and removes its `window.piDesktop` automation methods. Integrations that call those methods must switch to the Agents API; copying data does not keep the old commands running. The preload bridge is an application-internal interface, not a promised third-party plugin API.

## Workspace and provider changes

- **M3 Expressive** skin and an independent matching palette join Default and Angelcore. Roboto Flex is bundled locally. Existing per-skin font, color, and density preferences remain independent.
- The window has a fullscreen control. The composer distinguishes Stop from Queue follow-up during a live run.
- A plain **Expand details / Collapse details** action on the left of the extension-status row opens or closes every reasoning and tool call, including offscreen history. Individual rows still open or close on their own; changing sessions resets the bulk view. Ctrl+O remains reserved for Open.
- OpenAI-compatible custom provider defaults are safer for aggregator endpoints. File changes to Fate-owned `models.json` and `auth.json` refresh live provider state; removing a stored API key clears its runtime override. Invalid partial auth writes do not wipe live keys.
- Agent Team scheduling no longer imposes the earlier arbitrary team-size ceiling. Permission, workspace ownership, and bounded message/tool admission remain enforced.

## Install and trust

The planned native artifact set is Windows x64 EXE; macOS Apple Silicon/Intel DMG and PKG; Linux x64 AppImage and DEB; plus `SHA256SUMS`. Installers remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized. Verify the checksum for your downloaded asset; checksums do not replace code signing. Fate UI is local-first, not offline-only: prompts and selected context go to your configured provider. Full access is unsandboxed; worktrees are not security sandboxes.

Publishing is gated on the native four-runner package/install/smoke matrix and an exact seven-installer checksum set. A Windows-only local test pass is not cross-platform release approval.

name: V1.0.0 - Modulo
body:
# V1.0.0 - Modulo

**Fate UI 1.0 brings the real Pi coding agent into a complete desktop workspace.** Modulo is the first stable release: one place to plan a change, delegate work, supply useful context, inspect the result, and decide what to ship.

Fate UI embeds the Pi SDK directly. There is no terminal UI scraping and no separate Pi terminal installation to manage.

![Fate UI workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/v1.0.0/screenshots/fate-ui-dark.png)

*Actual Electron UI with a local demonstration project and illustrative agent messages.*

## One workspace for the coding session

### Agents and workflows, together

Individual agents, recursive delegation, and dependency-based workflows now use one execution engine. There is no Legacy/Teams mode selector.

Choose each agent's model, reasoning effort, profile, tools, and skills. Use the shared checkout or a managed Git worktree according to the global workspace preference. Review changes before explicitly integrating them; completion alone does not merge code or remove a worktree.

The agent inspector keeps task state, messages, usage, and workspace ownership visible. Retained context supports follow-up work, while historical standalone records remain available without being silently revived as live agents.

### Browser context that points to the right thing

The embedded browser keeps relevant pages beside the conversation. Select page elements and attach annotations so the agent can work from specific context instead of a vague description. Browser control has explicit origin and interaction policies; it is not arbitrary desktop control.

### Git, files, and a separate terminal

Browse project files, inspect Monaco diffs, review Git history and working-tree changes, and use a manual terminal without leaving the workspace. Activity views connect runtime events and direct-write records to the investigation, while preserving the distinction between related activity and proof of authorship.

### Longer goals without invisible state

GoalMax pairs objectives with criteria, tasks, evidence, and verification. The compact task/goal rails expose the next step; the Flight Deck provides the detail. Pending workflow admission and live parent/child joins prevent premature completion.

Queues preserve editable drafts and their delivery mode. Steering, follow-ups, saved instructions, and uncertain recovered messages remain visible; uncertain delivery is not blindly replayed after restart.

### A workspace that fits the way you work

- **Default and Angelcore skins**, independent palettes and fonts, imported skin packs, and locally processed dithered backgrounds.
- **Consistent compact controls** across queue, tasks, steering, and GoalMax, plus proper confirmation dialogs and keyboard-operable menus.
- **Opt-in Memory Learning** for reviewed global coding preferences and project-specific notes/procedures.
- **Local voice transcription**, optional image generation, and a separate ambient-audio player.
- **Multiple projects, durable sessions, branches, session references, and direct session messages.**

## Reliability work behind V1

Modulo separates execution from notification and cleanup. A successful task is not automatically rerun because its result could not be delivered. Follow-ups do not overwrite an unfinished parent/child join. Failed-to-stop work retains its writer lease until actual settlement, and cancellation attempts all requested targets before reporting failures.

Workflow runtime/idle/resource checkpoints remain advisory rather than hidden stop rules. Agent admission, workspace ownership, and history/transport bounds remain explicit.

The Pi SDK pin is **0.85.1**, verified against the upstream GitHub release. V1 keeps the tested public SDK and Fate's stronger application-owned queue, trust, and orchestration boundaries instead of importing unreleased upstream experiments.

## Versioning

The application displays **V1.0.0 - Modulo**. The machine version is **`1.0.0`**.

Tags, installer filenames, checksums, and update ordering use the version number. The release name is display metadata: a future `1.0.1` is newer regardless of its name, and a name-only change does not create an update.

## Installation and upgrade

Artifacts target:

| Platform | Architecture | Formats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | x64 | EXE |
| macOS | Apple Silicon and Intel | DMG, PKG |
| Linux | x64 | AppImage, DEB |

Download the installer for your platform and the accompanying `SHA256SUMS`. Existing local sessions, settings, and provider data are retained. Earlier standalone agent records remain historical; newly created work uses the unified runtime. Recovered workflows and uncertain message delivery still require the appropriate explicit recovery action.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **These installers remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized.** Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper may warn or block launch. Verify downloads against the published `SHA256SUMS` and review platform trust prompts. Checksums do not replace publisher code signing.

## Trust and limits

Fate UI is local-first, not offline-only. Prompts and selected context go to your configured AI provider. Full access is intentionally unsandboxed, and a Git worktree is not a security sandbox. Keep important work backed up and review changes before merging or deploying them.

Automated checks and model-assisted verification do not guarantee that every generated change is correct. Native release artifacts are gated by the platform build/smoke matrix; runtime/provider failures remain visible rather than being called success.

[Get started](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui#download) · [Documentation](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/tree/v1.0.0/docs) · [Agent orchestration](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v1.0.0/docs/agent-orchestration.md) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/issues)

# Fate UI v0.9.9-beta1

You should not have to re-explain how you like to work, or what this repository already decided, every time you open a new session. This release adds opt-in Memory Learning: reviewed notes you can inspect, change, and turn off.

## Turn it on in Settings

Open **Settings → Memory Learning**:

- **Enable** is off by default. Turning it off stops new capture and attachment; stored files stay on disk.
- **GLOBAL** is your coding profile across trusted projects.
- **PROJECT** is this repository’s briefing and notes.
- **Review → Open** is the library: edit, approve, and see what was actually attached. It is not a third kind of memory.

Nothing is written into the git checkout. Fate UI does not train the model or infer a psychological profile. Your current instructions still win.

## What gets remembered

GLOBAL holds one reviewed user profile: communication, workflow, taste, likes, and dislikes. PROJECT can hold a briefing plus ordinary notes and procedures. After you set a store to Automatic, later sessions can receive the approved profile and briefing without picking them again. Task-specific notes still need a match. Briefings that list current work or next steps need review after a week, so stale progress is not treated as fact.

A record of each attachment is kept so you can see the exact revisions that were handed to the runtime. That is not proof the provider received the request or followed the note.

## Compatibility and downloads

Upgrading keeps Memory Learning off until you enable it. Existing conversations are not rewritten; start a fresh session if you want to avoid older context.

# Fate UI v0.9.8-beta5

Workspace preferences should be set before the AI starts delegating, not on each team afterward. This release moves that choice into Settings and removes the manual setup from Run → Agents.

## Set it once in Settings

Open **Settings → Agent → Subagent workspaces**:

- **Prefer isolated worktrees** is on by default. Turn it off to prefer a shared checkout instead.
- **Strict mode** is off by default. Leave it off to let the agent choose the other workspace mode when a task calls for it. Turn it on to require your chosen mode: incompatible launches and resumed work are refused by the backend.

Changes apply after saving, including to future work in teams that already exist. You do not need to stop the AI, create a team, or reopen the project to change the workspace policy. Running turns stay in their current checkout; existing work is never moved or discarded by a settings change.

## A quieter Agents panel

The per-team workspace defaults form and manual **New team** button are gone. The AI creates teams as needed. Run → Agents remains the place to follow their activity, review changes, make checkpoints, integrate approved commits, and clean up retained worktrees.

## For agent-driven workflows

`get_agent_workspace_policy` reports the current preference and strict flag. Per-spawn workspace, base-ref, and branch choices remain available within that policy. The old `configure_agent_workspace` tool is no longer exposed, and beta4 team defaults cannot override the global setting.

Workspace tool replies now include the checkout and bounded review details in text the agent can read. Reviews too large for that context remain blocked from integration until reviewed through the UI. Strict-refused follow-ups and direct-message turns are recorded as failed instead of being left queued to run later.

Automatic GoalMax reviews use the current project checkout when policy is flexible. Strict isolated reviews require a clean, committed project, so verification does not accidentally inspect an older version of your work.

Workspace policy applies to **Agent Teams V2**. Legacy subagents keep their existing behavior, and the selected orchestration protocol is not changed by this update. Upgrading preserves other settings and starts the new workspace preference with isolated worktrees preferred and Strict mode off.

A worktree is still not an operating-system sandbox; Full access remains unsandboxed. Git requirements, explicit review/integration, and safe cleanup checks still apply.

# Fate UI v0.9.8-beta4

Agents can now work in separate local Git worktrees instead of sharing every file in your project. The parent reviews their changes and decides what comes back. Shared checkouts are still the default; nothing gets merged just because an agent says it is finished.

## What's new

- **Optional worktrees for Agent Teams V2.** Choose the workspace per agent, including its base revision and branch, or set defaults for the team. Agents in separate worktrees can write in parallel; writers sharing a checkout still take turns.
- **Workspace review in Run → Agents.** Open an agent's workspace to see its checkout, branch, parent target, diff, and commits. Create a local checkpoint, fast-forward the parent, or cherry-pick selected commits after reviewing them.
- **Explicit cleanup.** Closing or releasing an agent keeps its worktree and branch. Removing a worktree is a separate action that refuses to discard uncommitted work, ignored files, or retained descendant worktrees. The branch stays available.
- **Task statuses are no longer clickable toggles.** The agent updates progress. You can still cancel an ordinary task, but clicking “To do,” “In progress,” or “Blocked” will not change its state.

## Safeguards

Integration checks the reviewed commits and parent branch again before changing files. Checkout locks cover review, integration, cleanup, and worktree creation. Conflicting cherry-pick sequences are aborted rather than leaving an earlier part of the sequence applied.

Worktree sessions inherit the approved root's settings and skill catalog. Git operations disable repository hooks, external filters, custom merge drivers, and signing programs. Restored workspaces are checked against their owner, parent checkout, repository, branch, and original base commit.

## Compatibility

This feature is available in **Agent Teams V2**, not legacy subagent mode. Existing shared-checkout sessions keep their behavior. A worktree isolates checked-out files, not the operating system: **Full access remains unsandboxed**, and unrelated shells or application processes are outside Fate's checkout locks.

See [Agent orchestration](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/blob/v0.9.8-beta4/docs/agent-orchestration.md) for the controls and tool examples.

The release pipeline verifies and smoke-tests native installers on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64 before publishing. Choose the installer for your system below.

# Fate UI v0.9.8-beta1

This beta adds recovery for queued messages, makes GoalMax completion checks stricter, and brings task tools to ordinary sessions.

## Changes since v0.9.7-beta4

- Queued messages and messages held during compaction are saved before Fate hands them to Pi. After a restart, unacknowledged messages appear as saved drafts for review. Fate does not resend them automatically. Restoring a draft also restores its available model and reasoning settings; the saved copy stays until you discard it.
- Stop now cancels queued and held messages and prevents a message still waiting for a disk write from starting afterward. Compaction callbacks cannot submit the same held message twice. Editing a waiting message retains a saved copy so a session switch does not lose the draft.
- Agent Team messages distinguish dispatching from acknowledged delivery. A message is acknowledged when the recipient session records it, rather than when an in-memory handoff returns. Interrupted dispatches require transcript review before another send.
- GoalMax user messages use the normal session queue, including attachments, editing, cancellation, and steering controls. New user work takes priority over automatic continuation and prevents stale verification from completing a goal. Required criteria must be satisfied and have current supporting evidence.
- GoalMax preserves buffered evidence when saving fails. Corrupt snapshots and missing or altered goal briefs now report restoration errors instead of appearing to be absent goals. Archive operations preserve the active brief until the current snapshot has been removed.
- Ordinary sessions can list, create, update, and delete tasks through agent tools. GoalMax still manages its own generated tasks.
- Goal and task rows take less space, including in Compact mode. Clicking the goal title opens the Flight Deck; saved goal instructions are collapsed separately from waiting messages. The Main agent header also fits better in narrow panels.
- Agent Team spawning rejects malformed explicit models, unsupported tools or reasoning levels, and tools excluded by the chosen agent profile. Existing exact-model selection and permission limits remain in place.
- Developers can use two new offline component-task evaluations for message recovery and exact model routing. The grader retains acceptance results and source hashes, checks for regressions against a compatible baseline, and keeps grading time separate from externally reported task time and provider cost.

## Scope and recovery notes

Queued-draft recovery does not resume interrupted tool calls or guarantee exactly-once external effects. Check the recipient transcript before resending a message whose delivery is uncertain. Saved outbox drafts and attachments are local plaintext, like session data, and each application instance has its own outbox.

This release does not add a unified completion-evidence bundle, role-routing settings, managed agent worktree integration, automation Run now, or scheduling. The offline evaluation fixtures do not establish live-provider quality or cost improvements.

## Downloads and verification

The release pipeline runs native checks, builds, and installer smoke tests on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64 before publishing. Downloads include a Windows installer, DMG and PKG installers for both Mac architectures, and Linux AppImage and DEB packages.
