# Fate UI v0.9.7-beta4

This beta fixes session navigation races, misleading activity in restored sessions, and local file links in chat.

## Changes since v0.9.7-beta3

- Opening a folder and selecting or creating a session now happen in one queued operation. Rapid clicks no longer leave a session request competing with another folder change. The sidebar ignores stale responses and duplicate in-flight clicks, and you can move to another folder while session creation finishes.
- The built-in browser now waits for its first tab to finish initializing before accepting navigation. This fixes a startup race that could leave local previews blank on macOS.
- Restored tool calls without a recorded result no longer appear to be running. They show an interruption notice instead. Opening a saved session does not resume those calls; running indicators require live execution events.
- Local file links in assistant messages now reveal the file in your system file manager. Relative paths, local file URLs, Windows paths, and sandbox-prefixed paths work when they resolve to a file inside the active project. Missing files produce an error, and paths outside the project remain blocked. Clicking a link does not execute the file.

# Fate UI v0.9.7-beta3

This beta updates the embedded Pi SDK to 0.85.0, reduces streaming overhead, and fixes session handling and navigation. The base version remains 0.9.7.

## Changes since v0.9.7-beta2

- Saved-session references restore through the SDK's new in-memory API. Tagging a session no longer migrates or repairs its file. References respect the active branch, support compaction checkpoints, redact secrets, and reject stale identities or cyclic paths.
- Basic Prompt Optimization uses the selected model without inheriting the coding session's extended reasoning budget. Advanced Prompt Improvement keeps its research step and settings. Cancelling a stalled rewrite releases the composer without aborting the coding session.
- Stop now cancels manual SDK compaction too.
- Unchanged assistant Markdown no longer reparses on unrelated renders. Performance mode disables transitions completely and batches provisional output for up to 64 ms; Holy sh*t uses up to 200 ms. Buffers have fixed limits, coalesce redundant tool snapshots, and preserve cursor ordering. Completion, errors, queues, provenance, and session changes remain immediate.
- Height-driven scrolling replaces the repeated settling loop and delayed auto-scroll callbacks. New prompts follow correctly when their response or first tool arrives in the same batch; manual scrolling stays in control. End targets the final virtual item instead of an estimated scroll height.
- Disposed hydration requests and buffered events cannot replay into a different session. The manual fork smoke launcher uses a private profile instead of deleting shared instance profiles.

## Dependencies and verification

Electron moves to 43.6.0 and the speech runtime to 0.2.3, alongside compatible rendering and test-package updates. Radix popover stays on 1.1.22 after its newer patch failed the permission-picker test. yt-dlp was already on the latest stable release, 2026.08.19. Framework major versions remain unchanged.

The update includes regression tests for all three performance modes, SDK restoration, cancellation, event bounds, cursor ordering, and navigation. Native workflows verify Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64. A non-promotion manual run stages seven installers and `SHA256SUMS` for 14 days without creating a tag or publishing a release.

Public beta installers are unsigned. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.

# Fate UI v0.9.6-beta3

A follow-up build for the 0.9.6 beta.

## Fixed

- **macOS in-app update.** The updater now installs the bundle under the name actually shipped inside the DMG (`fate-ui.app`) and relaunches the executable it verified inside that bundle. Earlier betas assumed `Fate UI.app`, so the download reached 100% but the relaunch failed and the app stayed open (or crashed with `spawn ... ENOENT`).
- **Nested installs.** If the old bundle could not be removed (for example a PKG install owned by the system), the update now stops with a clear instruction to install manually instead of copying the new bundle inside the old one.
- **Update relaunch failures are reported.** A failed relaunch now shows the update error in the app instead of an uncaught-exception dialog, and the app no longer quits when nothing was relaunched.
- **Legacy cleanup.** Leftover `Fate UI.app` bundles from earlier broken updates are removed after a successful install.

# Fate UI v0.9.6-beta1

A feature prerelease: a device emulation toolbar for the browser pane, annotate rebuilt as an always-available picker, and a composer that forgives mistakes.

## Added

- **Device emulation toolbar.** The browser pane can now masquerade as a phone. A new toolbar row offers Chrome-style presets (iPhone SE through iPad Pro 11) plus exact width and height inputs, a rotate button, and translated touch input: while emulation is on, mouse events reach the page as finger touches, so mobile-only gesture handlers behave like they would on a real device. Emulation applies to every open tab at once and survives tab switches; one toggle restores desktop input.
- **Draft undo and redo in the composer.** Each conversation keeps its own history (up to 100 snapshots) and restores the cursor position and scroll offset, not just the text.

## Changed

- **Annotate is now a tool, not a mode.** The Agent/Annotate segmented switch is gone. Annotate became a toolbar toggle that runs the element picker as an overlay: agent interaction stays fully enabled while you annotate, and site access prompts now appear only when an origin grant is actually missing. Toggling annotate off returns direct clicks; Esc cancels a pick.
- **Pickers wait as long as you do.** Element picks and region drags no longer time out after 60 seconds; they stay armed until you click, drag, or cancel, like Chrome DevTools. When Chromium keeps dropping the picker, a bounded retry budget (12 re-arms) lets the loop rest instead of spinning every 250 ms forever.
- **Send button, rebuilt.** The hold-to-abort gesture is gone. The send button now shows a stop square while the agent runs with an empty input, and the prompt optimizer shows its spinner with a cancel on hover.
- **Auto-scroll settles after big prompts.** The conversation keeps following the bottom for a short settling window after you submit, so very large prompt rows finish measuring instead of stranding the view mid-jump. Manual scrolling still wins instantly.
- **Music dock yields to the browser pane.** When the browser pane shares the workspace above 820 px, the floating music dock slides left instead of covering the pane's toggle; below that width the pane stacks under the conversation and the dock keeps its corner.

## Fixed

- **Annotations survive project switches.** The annotation store no longer lives inside the disposable browser service. It is kept per normalized project path (bounded, six projects), so unsent annotation chips keep pointing at real data across focus switches, worktree activation, tab closes, and service rebuilds.
- **Stale annotations no longer break sends.** When the main process rejects a prompt because attached annotations are gone, the composer extracts the offending ids from the error and drops them from the draft instead of failing every later prompt.
- **Overlay numbers match the input box.** The browser overlay numbering now mirrors the composer's attachment list per conversation and resets after every send, so the two never disagree.

## Verification

- Local validation: TypeScript typecheck, the full unit suite (157 files, 1498 tests), and a production build.
- GitHub Actions runs the standard four-platform pipeline: build, install, and smoke test on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64.

## Notes

- Public beta installers are unsigned. Verify each download against the `SHA256SUMS` file shipped with the release.

# Fate UI v0.9.5-beta1

A feature prerelease: model visibility controls, a smarter voice gate, compact layout polish, and a full dependency refresh.

## Added

- **Per-model visibility.** Every provider now has a models dialog in Settings where individual models can be hidden. Hidden models disappear from the model picker, the command palette, and the subagent catalog, and a disabled model can no longer be the default. Subagent spawning and team coordinators respect the same list, so hidden models fail fast with a clear message instead of erroring deep inside a run.
- **Compaction section in Settings.** Message density controls moved to their own place, so tuning how dense the transcript renders no longer lives under appearance.
- **Performance CI.** The renderer now gets profiled in CI so search and rendering regressions are caught before a release.

## Changed

- **Smarter local dictation.** The silence gate now works on 30 ms frames with a pre-roll buffer and a hangover tail, ported from Handy's SmoothedVad design. Word onsets are no longer clipped, thinking pauses do not feed the decoder, and Windows, macOS, and Linux share one PCM path with no extra native dependency.
- **Compact mode polish.** Header and browser-pane actions now clear the fixed window-controls strip on Windows and Linux when the inspector is collapsed, and the draggable header regions were split so dragging works without fighting the buttons.
- **Sessions survive a crash.** The active session is kept after a renderer crash instead of being dropped on restart.

## Dependencies

- **yt-dlp 2026.08.19** (from 2026.07.04): YouTube, TikTok, Apple, and Instagram extractor fixes, plus a refreshed third-party license bundle. All pins re-verified against the signed release checksums.
- **lucide-react 1.x** (from 0.468): the GitHub brand icon was removed upstream, so the commit card now carries the official GitHub mark inline.
- **transcribe-cpp 0.2.1** (from 0.1.3): diarization support, a `rocm` backend, and opaque device handles. Fate UI never used the removed `gpuDevice` API, so no migration was needed.
- **dompurify 3.4.14** (allow-list bypass fix), **mermaid 11.17**, **electron 43.4.1**, **vite 8.2.2**, **vitest 4.1.11**, **jest-dom 7**, **cross-env 10**, plus Radix UI, typebox, react-virtuoso, and testing-library patches.
- **@radix-ui/react-popover is held at 1.1.22** because 1.1.23 carries an upstream regression (radix-ui/primitives#4124) that breaks popover content. It moves once upstream fixes it.

- Local validation: TypeScript typecheck, the full unit suite (156 files, 1475 tests), a production build, and the end-to-end Electron suite (4 specs).
